newsitem.title: BRAZIL: VW aims to stay Brazil mkt leader-paper.
newsitem.headline: VW aims to stay Brazil mkt leader-paper.

text.p: Volkswagen AG's Brazilian unit, its largest subsidiary outside Germany, aims to maintain its 40-year leadership in the country's car market, a local financial newspaper said.
"We think, with all modesty, that we are in a position to continue leading," the unit's president, Alain De Smedt, told Gazeta Mercantil in an interview.
In 1996's first eleven months, Volkswagen produced 536,000 cars in Brazil, or 35 percent of Brazil's total auto output.

Fiat SpA was second with 413,000 cars assembled in the country, or a 27 percent market share, it said. De Smedt also was quoted as saying that Brazil was one of the most profitable countries for automakers, with average profitability of five percent of gross revenues.

He said Volkswagen was studying the creation of a sub-compact car to compete with Ford Motor Co's Ka model although the firm did not plan to produce the vehicle in Brazil, according to Gazeta. "We would have to sacrifice our margins," De Smedt was quoted as saying.
Meanwhile, Volkswagen and its unit Audi announced today they will invest 750 million marks to build a new car plant in Brazil to produce Vento and Audi A3 cars.
